clinician.final_diagnosis: chronic nonunion of a medial condyle fracture
clinician.trajectory_summary: A six-year-old male presented with a left elbow dislocation after failed reduction attempts at an outside facility. The elbow was successfully reduced under ketamine sedation. Serial radiographs obtained immediately post-reduction (E001), at 5 days (E002), at 1 week (E003), and at 6 weeks (E004) all demonstrated a well-reduced elbow without apparent fracture. At the 6-week timepoint, additional ossification at the medial epicondyle and possible heterotopic ossification from multiple reduction attempts were noted. The patient returned to normal function. At five years post-injury, the patient presented with a new, unrelated metacarpal fracture and reported approximately six months of intermittent medial elbow discomfort with popping during pushups. Physical examination revealed mild tenderness along the medial elbow with limited range of motion (25-130 degrees). This clinical presentation and timeline are consistent with an occult medial condyle fracture that was not radiographically apparent on the initial serial imaging studies but subsequently failed to unite, resulting in chronic nonunion. The nonunion became clinically manifest by the five-year mark with mechanical symptoms and functional limitations.
